citation.title: Optimisation of three-dimensional hierarchical structures with tailored lattice metamaterial anisotropy
citation.authors: Lei Zhu, Liao Sun, Xiao-Yang Wang, Nan Li
citation.version_coded: Abstract only. Both the ScienceDirect article page and its /pdf route (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521006389 and .../pdf) returned HTTP 403 with an Elsevier 'IP blocked' bot-detection page (not a login/paywall message) to scripted access; the doi.org redirect chain ends at the same linkinghub.elsevier.com meta-refresh page seen to block other ScienceDirect articles in this queue. Per Semantic Scholar's record (queried via its open API, not Elsevier), this article is Gold Open Access under a CC-BY licence, so the block is a bot check, not a paywall - it was not bypassed. A web search found no legal alternate copy (only a ResearchGate page, which is excluded by the access rules). The abstract text used here is the publisher's own abstract as indexed by Semantic Scholar's open API (api.semanticscholar.org), not a third-party paraphrase

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Abstract: using ANN surrogates for the homogenised properties of lattice metamaterials, optimised 3D hierarchical structures with tailored anisotropic lattices are reported to give 'superior structural efficiency' compared with classical topology optimisation and with quasi-isotropic lattice optimisation, with no numeric margin stated.
claim.key_phrase: optimised structures composed of tailored anisotropic lattice metamaterials achieved superior structural efficiency
claim.location: abstract (the only text accessible; full text could not be checked)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not stated in the abstract. The abstract frames the neural-network surrogate as improving 'computational efficiency' of the optimisation framework generally, but gives no time, iteration-count, or cost figure for either the surrogate-based or the classical topology-optimisation comparator.
claim.alternatives: The abstract separately claims the ANN surrogate 'improve[s] the computational efficiency of the framework' relative to (presumably) repeated full numerical homogenisation, and that the optimised strut-radii distributions 'approximately align with the paths of the principal stresses' - both qualitative, unquantified statements. Without full text it cannot be determined which comparison (vs. classical topology optimisation, vs. quasi-isotropic lattice optimisation, or the computational-efficiency claim) the article itself treats as primary, nor whether any of them is given numbers in the body text.

baseline.classical_method: Not stated beyond 'classical topology optimisation' and 'optimising quasi-isotropic lattice metamaterials', named as the two comparators in the abstract; no specific algorithm (SIMP/level-set/etc.) is given
baseline.implementation: not stated; the abstract mentions 'a new platform integrating user-defined functions with multiple robust and efficient commercial software' but names no specific package
baseline.solver: not stated; the abstract states effective lattice properties are obtained by 'numerical homogenisation'
baseline.problem_size: not stated numerically; the abstract mentions 'three case studies featuring multiple lattice types and configurations' with no element/DOF counts
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; the ANN surrogate presumably requires homogenisation data over a range of strut radii, but no sample count or generation cost is given in the abstract
baseline.quality_metric: not stated numerically; the abstract's only stated quality indicator is qualitative ('superior structural efficiency') plus a descriptive observation that optimised strut-radii distributions align with principal-stress paths
baseline.quality_gap: not quantified in the abstract; only the qualitative claim of superior structural efficiency for tailored-anisotropic-lattice structures versus classical topology optimisation and quasi-isotropic lattice optimisation

reporting.n_test_cases: not verifiable beyond the abstract's 'three case studies featuring multiple lattice types and configurations'

notes: Coded from the abstract only, per the protocol's abstract-only fallback. The doi.org redirect and a web search for an alternate legal copy (only ResearchGate was found, which is excluded by the access rules) did not help. Per instructions, the article is kept as include with reason 'I-UNCLEAR (no accessible full text)', stratum set to 'none', and all four rules set to na with evidence 'no full text', even though the abstract itself names two classical comparators (classical topology optimisation; quasi-isotropic lattice optimisation) and claims 'superior structural efficiency' - it gives no numeric margin for either comparison, so this would likely have been an I-QUALITY case at full text. method_family is coded surrogate_mlp_gp (the abstract explicitly names 'artificial neural network based surrogate models' for the lattice metamaterials' effective properties) and physics as metamaterial_homogenization (the abstract explicitly uses 'numerical homogenisation' to characterise the lattice metamaterials' effective properties).
